name: Microsoft Defender XDR
description: Microsoft Defender XDR: incidents, alerts, advanced hunting query results, machines and attack simulations, across the five Splunk sourcetypes the Microsoft Defender TAs write.
source: Microsoft Learn API and advanced hunting schema references (defender-xdr, defender-endpoint, microsoft graph security), read against the repo's own seeded samples and entry.json transform notes.

feed.label: Microsoft Defender XDR
feed.description: Microsoft Defender XDR across five shapes: streamed Advanced Hunting events, Microsoft 365 Defender incidents, ad hoc Advanced Hunting query results, Defender for Endpoint machines and Attack simulation and training campaigns.

envelope_receive_time.label: Event Hub receive time
envelope_receive_time.description: When Defender XDR received the event and wrote it to the Event Hub, the envelope's own time field.

tenant_id.label: Tenant id
tenant_id.description: The Microsoft Entra tenant the record belongs to, a GUID.

record_category.label: Advanced Hunting category
record_category.description: The Advanced Hunting table name the streamed record came from, prefixed AdvancedHunting-. Only one value (AdvancedHunting-AlertEvidence) is in the sample; Microsoft's page describes the prefix convention, not a closed list of tables.

operation_name.label: Operation name
operation_name.description: A label alongside category on the streamed record. Not in Microsoft's own event-hub envelope docs, which show only time, tenantId, category and properties; only in the Splunk-published concrete example this sample is drawn from, so the meaning is read off the field name, not vendor-confirmed.
operation_name.notes: Not named by streaming_eventhub; worked out from the field name and its position alongside category.

envelope_tenant_label.label: Tenant label
envelope_tenant_label.description: A short tenant label on the streamed record (observed value DefaultTenant), distinct from the tenantId GUID. Not documented by Microsoft's envelope page.
envelope_tenant_label.notes: Not named by streaming_eventhub; only in the Splunk-published sample.

alert_time.label: Alert evidence time
alert_time.description: Date and time when the AlertEvidence event was recorded.

alert_id.label: Alert id
alert_id.description: Unique identifier for the alert the evidence row belongs to.

alert_categories.label: Alert categories
alert_categories.description: List of categories the alert belongs to, as a JSON array in a string.

attack_techniques.label: MITRE ATT&CK techniques
attack_techniques.description: MITRE ATT&CK techniques associated with the activity that triggered the alert.

service_source.label: Service source
service_source.description: Product or service that provided the alert information. Microsoft names no closed list; the sample shows Microsoft Defender for Cloud.

detection_source.label: Detection source
detection_source.description: Detection technology or sensor that identified the notable component or activity. Microsoft names no closed list; the sample shows DefenderForServers.

entity_type.label: Entity type
entity_type.description: Type of object the evidence row is about: a file, a process, a device, a user, and so on. Microsoft names no closed list; the sample shows CloudResource.

evidence_role.label: Evidence role
evidence_role.description: How the entity is involved in the alert: impacted, or merely related. The sample shows Impacted.

evidence_direction.label: Evidence direction
evidence_direction.description: Whether the entity is the source or the destination of a network connection. Null on every row of the sample (a CloudResource entity, not a network one).

alert_severity.label: Alert severity
alert_severity.description: The potential impact of the threat indicator or breach activity the alert identifies: high, medium or low. The sample shows High.

device_id.label: Device id
device_id.description: Unique identifier for the device in the Defender service. A 40-character lowercase hex string, the same shape as a SHA-1 hash.

device_name.label: Device name
device_name.description: Fully qualified domain name of the device.

remote_ip.label: Remote address
remote_ip.description: The IP address that was being connected to.

local_ip.label: Local address
local_ip.description: The IP address assigned to the local device used during the communication.

remote_url.label: Remote URL
remote_url.description: URL or fully qualified domain name that was being connected to.

account_object_id.label: Account object id
account_object_id.description: Unique identifier for the account in Microsoft Entra ID.

account_upn.label: Account UPN
account_upn.description: User principal name of the account.

network_message_id.label: Network message id
network_message_id.description: Unique identifier for the email, generated by Office 365.

application_name.label: Application name
application_name.description: Application that performed the recorded action.

application_id.label: Application id
application_id.description: Unique identifier for the application (an int, on AlertEvidence).

oauth_application_id.label: OAuth application id
oauth_application_id.description: Unique identifier of the third-party OAuth application.

process_command_line.label: Process command line
process_command_line.description: Command line used to create the new process. The same field on AlertEvidence and on DeviceProcessEvents.

registry_key.label: Registry key
registry_key.description: Registry key that the recorded action was applied to.

registry_value_name.description: Name of the registry value that the recorded action was applied to.

registry_value_data.label: Registry value data
registry_value_data.description: Data of the registry value that the recorded action was applied to.

additional_fields.description: Additional information about the entity or event, as a JSON object encoded in a string.

file_name.description: Name of the file that the recorded action was applied to.

folder_path.label: Folder path
folder_path.description: Folder containing the file that the recorded action was applied to.

file_hash_sha1.label: File SHA-1

file_hash_sha256.label: File SHA-256

file_size.description: Size of the file in bytes.

threat_family.label: Threat family
threat_family.description: Malware family that the suspicious or malicious file or process has been classified under.

hunting_time.label: Advanced hunting event time
hunting_time.description: Date and time when the process event was recorded.

initiating_process_file_name.label: Initiating process file name
initiating_process_file_name.description: Name of the process file that initiated the event; if unavailable, the name of the process that initiated the event might be shown instead.

initiating_process_folder_path.label: Initiating process folder path
initiating_process_folder_path.description: Folder containing the process (image file) that initiated the event.

initiating_process_command_line.label: Initiating process command line
initiating_process_command_line.description: Command line used to run the process that initiated the event.

recipient_email_address.label: Recipient email address
recipient_email_address.description: An email recipient address on a DeviceProcessEvents row (present via AdditionalFields on email-related process events). Not in the table's own column list; the sample carries it as a top-level field the TA lifted out.
recipient_email_address.notes: Not a documented DeviceProcessEvents column; kept from the CIM layer the TA applies, meaning read off the field name.

process_guid.label: Process GUID
process_guid.description: A process's unique id on the device, distinct from the recycled OS process id.
process_guid.notes: Standard CIM process_guid field; not a documented DeviceProcessEvents or AlertEvidence column, read off the field name and the CIM convention.

process_integrity_level.label: Process integrity level
process_integrity_level.description: Integrity level of the process, which Windows assigns based on how it was launched and which influences its permissions.

parent_process_name.label: Parent process name
parent_process_name.description: Name of the parent process that spawned the process responsible for the event.

parent_process_path.label: Parent process path
parent_process_path.description: Folder path of the parent process.
parent_process_path.notes: CIM parent_process_path alias; DeviceProcessEvents documents InitiatingProcessParentFileName by name only, not a folder path, so this is read off the CIM field name.

parent_process_id.label: Parent process id
parent_process_id.description: Process ID (PID) of the parent process that spawned the process responsible for the event.

parent_process_guid.label: Parent process GUID
parent_process_guid.description: The parent process's unique id on the device.
parent_process_guid.notes: Standard CIM field; not a documented column, read off the field name and the CIM convention.

process_hash.label: Process hash
process_hash.description: A hash of the process image file responsible for the event (SHA-1, SHA-256 or MD5 depending on the source column the TA aliased).

parent_process_hash.label: Parent process hash
parent_process_hash.description: A hash of the parent process's image file.

process_current_directory.label: Process current directory
process_current_directory.description: The working directory of the process.
process_current_directory.notes: Standard CIM field; not a documented DeviceProcessEvents column.

eventhub_time_bases.text: Up to three different times sit on one eventhub record: the envelope's time (when Defender XDR received it), properties.Timestamp (the underlying event's own time) and _time (the TA's indexed time, parsed from properties.Timestamp). Delivery lag separates them; filter on properties.Timestamp for the event's own time.

device_id_hex40.text: A Defender device or machine id is 40 lowercase hex characters, the same length and alphabet as a SHA-1 hash. Do not confuse a device id column with a file hash column on the strength of its shape alone.

id_meanings_differ.text: id (and its look-alikes) means a different thing on every container in this family: an AlertEvidence AlertId (eventhub), a numeric incident id (ms365:defender:incident), a 40-hex device or machine id (machines, advanced hunting) and a simulation GUID (simulations). Never join across containers on a bare id or similarly-named field without checking which one it is.

simulations_time_broken.text: props.conf's TIME_PREFIX for ms:defender:simulations is written as the literal string 'lastModifiedDateTime' with the single quotes taken as part of the regex; the JSON spells the key in double quotes, so the prefix never matches. Every event on this sourcetype indexes at ingest time, not at its own lastModifiedDateTime. Confirmed empirically: loading the sample landed _time at load time, not at the event's 2021-01-01 timestamp.

machine_last_seen_not_ui.text: lastSeen is the time of the last full device report (about every 24 hours), not the last-seen value the Defender portal UI shows for the same device.

sha256_rarely_populated.text: Microsoft's own reference says this field is usually not populated; use the SHA1 column when available.

extraction_casing_drift.text: The TA's top-level extracted field can lowercase a PascalCase vendor enum value (severity was seen as "high" at top level, "High" in _raw); match on _raw or accept either case, not one alone.

alerts_two_schemas.text: Two unrelated Defender alert schemas share field names: the Defender for Endpoint alert (evidence{}, relatedUser, threatName) and the Defender XDR incident's embedded alert (devices{}, entities{}, serviceSource, providerAlertId). Classification, determination and status enums differ in membership between them even where casing matches.

evidence_verdict_numeric.text: The sample's entities{}.verdict multivalue held "5" alongside "Suspicious" on the same event: a raw numeric code leaking through instead of the vendor's string enum. Do not treat a bare digit here as the literal verdict.
